artifacts.summary: Confirms task 261's --jobs parallelism (COMPLETED, not PARTIAL) already discharges the parallel-safety dependency; identifies a deterministic (not ambient-load) nested-RUN_ALL_NESTED-inheritance bug in test-run-all-parallel.sh's case3 assertion, reproduced live; narrows deploy-headless.sh's callers from 16 mentions to exactly 2 genuine invokers (command-gate-out.sh, orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh), both of which already collapse exit 0/3 into one branch, and recommends an opt-in --skip-verify flag with a new distinct exit code over a narrowed --only-gate inline verify.

memory_candidates.content: run-all.sh (agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/tests/) unconditionally exports RUN_ALL_NESTED=1 for its own process before invoking any discovered suite, regardless of whether --jobs was passed or whether this run-all.sh instance is itself nested. Any suite that shells out to a copy of run-all.sh to measure genuine parallel speedup (as test-run-all-parallel.sh does) must explicitly `env -u RUN_ALL_NESTED` its own 'unguarded' baseline measurement, or that measurement silently inherits the forced-sequential guard from its parent whenever the suite is discovered and run as part of any outer run-all.sh battery -- producing a deterministic (not flaky) timing-assertion failure that is easy to misattribute to ambient host load.

When enumerating 'callers' of a script from grep/doc references in this repo, distinguish GENUINE invocation (bash .../script.sh in command position) from MENTION (a remedy string, comment, or doc pointer naming the script) before reasoning about exit-code contracts. For deploy-headless.sh specifically, only command-gate-out.sh and orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh genuinely execute it -- 14+ other files that reference its name only print a remedy message. test-lint-deploy-caller-wrap.sh already re-derives this genuine/mention classification from file contents every run and is the authoritative source, not a hardcoded list.
